arxiv-2208-07627.title: From pp-Waves to Galilean Spacetimes
arxiv-2208-07627.creator: José FIGUEROA-O’FARRILL a, Ross GRASSIE b and Stefan PROHAZKA a
arxiv-2208-07627.description: Abstract We exhibit all spatially isotropic homogeneous Galilean spacetimes of dimension ( n + 1 ) ≥ 4 (n+1)\geq 4 , including the novel torsional ones, as null reductions of homogeneous pp-wave spacetimes. We also show that the pp-waves are sourced by pure radiation fields and analyse their global properties.

arxiv-2306-09082.title: Behavioral Cloning via Search in Embedded Demonstration Dataset
arxiv-2306-09082.creator: Federico MalatoSchool of ComputingUniversity of Eastern FinlandJoensuu, Finland federico.malato@uef.fi, Florian LeopoldBielefeld UniversityBielefeld, Germany fleopold@techfak.uni-bielefeld.de Ville HautamäkiSchool of ComputingUniversity of Eastern FinlandJoensuu, Finland villeh@cs.uef.fi Andrew Meln
arxiv-2306-09082.description: Abstract Behavioural cloning uses a dataset of demonstrations to learn a behavioural policy. To overcome various learning and policy adaptation problems, we propose to use latent space to index a demonstration dataset, instantly access similar relevant experiences, and copy behavior from these situations.

arxiv-2410-03068.title: Triply Graded Link Homology for Coxeter Braids on 4 Strands
arxiv-2410-03068.creator: Joshua P. Turner
arxiv-2410-03068.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Joshua P. Turner. We compute the triply graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology for Coxeter braids on 4 strands. Introduction In Section 6 of [ 11 ] , the author uses a recursive process developed by Hogancamp and Elias in [ 2 ] to compute the triply-graded Khovanov Rozansky homology (also called HHH) for Coxeter braids on 3 strands, matching the result with the bigraded Hilbert series of a particular ideal in a polynomial ring.

arxiv-2411-09463.title: Teaching Program Decomposition in CS1: A Conceptual Framework for Improved Code Quality Conference: Proceedings of the 56th ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education V. 1; February 26-March 1, 2025; Pittsburgh, PA, USA Proceedings of the 56th ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science E
arxiv-2411-09463.creator: Georgiana Haldeman, Judah Robbins Bernal, Alec Wydra, Paul Denny
arxiv-2411-09463.description: Abstract . Program decomposition is essential for developing maintainable and efficient software, yet it remains a challenging skill to teach and learn in introductory programming courses. What does program decomposition for procedural CS1 programs entail? How can CS1 students improve the decomposition of their programs? What scaffolded exercises can instructors use to teach program decomposition skills?

arxiv-2501-14027.title: Bell nonlocality in quantum networks with unreliable sources: Loophole-free postelection via self-testing
arxiv-2501-14027.creator: Sadra Boreiri, Nicolas Brunner, Pavel Sekatski
arxiv-2501-14027.description: Abstract We discuss Bell nonlocality in quantum networks with unreliable sources. Our main result is a condition on the observed data which ensures that inconclusive events can be safely discarded, without introducing any loophole. More formally, we characterize the fair-sampling property for measurements in a network.

arxiv-2502-06067.title: Smooth Sailing: Lipschitz-Driven Uncertainty Quantification for Spatial Association
arxiv-2502-06067.creator: David R. Burt, Renato BerlinghieriStephen BatesTamara BroderickMIT LIDS {dburt,renb,s_bates,tamarab}@mit.edu
arxiv-2502-06067.description: Abstract Estimating associations between spatial covariates and responses — rather than merely predicting responses — is central to environmental science, epidemiology, and economics. For instance, public health officials might be interested in whether air pollution has a strictly positive association with a health outcome, and the magnitude of any effect.

arxiv-2509-02482.title: Multiomics Tissue Segmentation via Spatially-Informed Nested Biclustering Methods
arxiv-2509-02482.creator: Francesco Denti, Cecilia Balocchi, Vanna Denti, and Giulia Capitoli
arxiv-2509-02482.description: Abstract Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation Mass Spectrometry Imaging (MSI) is a powerful technique for spatially resolved molecular profiling and cancer biomarker discovery. Recent advances, including a novel multiomics workflow, enable multiple rounds of MSI on the same tissue section, extracting diverse molecular classes, e.g., lipids, peptides, and N-glycans, while preserving spatial resolution.

arxiv-2512-09559.title: A tensor phase theory with applications in multilinear control footnoteinfo
arxiv-2512-09559.creator: Chengdong Liu, Yimin Wei, Guofeng Zhang
arxiv-2512-09559.description: Abstract The purpose of this paper is to initiate a phase theory for tensors under the Einstein product, and explore its applications in multilinear control systems. Firstly, the sectorial tensor decomposition for sectorial tensors is derived, which allows us to define phases for sectorial tensors. A numerical procedure for computing phases of a sectorial tensor is also proposed.

pmc-10603986.title: Microwave Breast Sensing via Deep Learning for Tumor Spatial Localization by Probability Maps
pmc-10603986.creator: Marijn Borghouts, Michele Ambrosanio, Stefano Franceschini, Maria Maddalena Autorino, Vito Pascazio, Fabio Baselice, Alan Wang, Sibusiso Mdletshe, Brady Williamson, Guizhi Xu
pmc-10603986.description: Background: microwave imaging (MWI) has emerged as a promising modality for breast cancer screening, offering cost-effective, rapid, safe and comfortable exams. Methods: this study aims to generate an accurate tumor probability map directly from the scattering matrix.

pmc-12695143.title: Advances in surface-enhanced Raman scattering applications for precision agriculture: monitoring plant health and crop quality
pmc-12695143.creator: Ha Anh Nguyen, Dao Thi Nguyet Nga, To Dao Cuong, Mai Quan Doan, Anh-Tuan Le
pmc-12695143.description: Ensuring plant health and crop quality is vital for sustainable modern agriculture. Conventional detection methods for stress markers, contaminants, and pathogens are often constrained by labor-intensive procedures, bulky equipment, and reliance on centralized facilities, limiting real-time field monitoring. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a promising solution, providing rapid, ultrasensitive, and non-destructive analysis across plant, soil, and water matrices.

pmc-12979562.description: Phytophthora blight, manifested by root, stem, and fruit rot, caused by the oomycete Phytophthora capsici, is an important disease affecting Chili pepper production globally. RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and shared genetic resistance mechanisms across different tissues upon infection by the pathogen.

pmc-13140530.description: Background and HypothesisA sex difference in the clinical presentation of schizophrenia is well known. pmc-13469617.creator: Abdullah S. Alawam, R. Rajesh, Abhishek Kumar Verma, Abhishek Dadhich, V. Choudri, Hassan A. Rudayni, Mubarak A. Alamri, Manoj Kumar Bohra
pmc-13469617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The development of heterocyclic scaffolds with anticancer and antimicrobial potential remains an important pursuit in medicinal chemistry. Among these, 1,3,4-thiadiazole derivatives are notable for their structural adaptability and wide spectrum of biological activities. In this study, a novel thiadiazole derivative was synthesised through a two-step process involving the condensation of (R)-carvone with thiosemicarbazide followed by cyclisation with diarylnitrilimines, affording high yields of 86–87%.

pmc-13657481.title: When dengue is not the answer: diagnostic anchoring bias in febrile illnesses in conflict-affected settings
pmc-13657481.creator: Mumen Abdalazim Dafallah, Fatima Abdelmonem Yousif Mohamed, Eman Osama Mohammed Omer, Alaa Nasreldeen Yousif Ahmed, Eilaf AbdElmoneim Nour Elbasheir, Aya Khidir Elamin Dafaalla, Ibtehaj Modawi Musa Modawi
pmc-13657481.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dengue is an increasingly prevalent arboviral infection in tropical regions, with expanding geographic distribution and rising reports of atypical and severe manifestations, including neurological involvement. In endemic and resource-limited settings, particularly those affected by conflict, the widespread availability of rapid diagnostic tests and overlapping clinical presentations with other infectious diseases have led to a growing concern: diagnostic anchoring bias toward dengue. This bias may contribute to misdiagnosis, delayed treatment of alternative life-threatening conditions, and distorted public health data.
